results.name: Alternate Hammer Curl Seated Dumbbells
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides. Your palms should face each other (neutral grip).
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl the right dumbbell up towards your shoulder, maintaining the neutral grip with your palm facing inward.
Squeeze your bicep at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the same motion with your left arm, alternating between right and left arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight to avoid putting unnecessary strain on them during the curls.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Visualize the bicep contraction to enhance the mind-muscle connection for better results.
results.description: Alternate Hammer Curl Seated Dumbbells is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Alternating Biceps Hammer Curl Resistance Band
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band and hold one end in each hand, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your sides.
Curl one hand up toward your shoulder, keeping your palm facing in.
Lower it with control and curl the other side.
tips: Keep your upper arms still.
Widen your stance for more tension.
results.description: Alternating Biceps Hammer Curl Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Band Close-Grip Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart, and a Resistance band under your feet.
Hold the ends of the bands in your hands while keeping your arms straight and palms facing forward.
Raise the band by folding your arms to a 90° angle while taking your hands close to each other.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you curl the band towards your shoulders and inhale as you lower it back down.
Keep your elbows close to your body and avoid swinging them forward or backward.
results.description: Band Close-Grip Biceps Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Biceps Curl Close Grip

Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, maintaining the supinated grip with your palms facing upward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows stay stationary and close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.

results.name: Barbell Drag Curl (45 Degree View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using a supinated grip (palms facing up). Your hands should be about shoulder-width apart.
Begin by pulling your elbows back and curling the barbell up along your body, dragging it against your torso.
Continue to pull the barbell upward until it reaches chest level, keeping your elbows back and close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, maintaining control and keeping the barbell close to your torso. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows back to ensure the barbell stays close to your torso throughout the movement.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
